_meta.host: AMD Ryzen AI 7 350 w/ Radeon 860M (16 cores)
_meta.note:
Both benchmarks now run against a receiver that drains the aggregation channel. Previously neither set MaxBufferedGradients, leaving the overflow buffer at 0, so once the 10000-slot channel filled every further gradient was dropped and the numbers described a path that aggregated nothing. Neither logged warnings before this fix only because each client was too slow to fill the channel.

Progression for BatchForwarding (10 x 1000-dim gradients):
  9827786 ns / 10368 allocs  original
  5256936 ns / 10301 allocs  after sizing encodeGradient (PR #200)
  338578  ns / 294   allocs  after pre-sizing the batch body and bulk-reading decode

GradientForwarding (single gradient per call) measures 119614 ns / 28 allocs. The earlier 523805 ns / 1031 allocs figure was inflated by the same backpressure defect. Its cost is dominated by the synchronous 1-byte ACK -- SendGradient blocks on io.ReadFull for the peer's acknowledgement, which is one network round trip per gradient and a deliberate durability property. Encoding is only 5252 ns of the 119614; the batch-body and bulk-decode optimizations do not apply because it sends one gradient per call. Amortizing the round trip is what ForwardBatch is for.

Measured with each benchmark in its own process; running both in one `go test -bench` invocation saturates the shared receiver and inflates both.
